quotes.text: The more you glue together different tools and manual scripts, the more you're inviting things to go sideways.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Names the core risk of patchwork ETL across many tools.

quotes.text: Every transformation, every filter, every join is just code, easy to review, debug and repeat if you need to fix something or explain it to an auditor.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Sums up why code-based notebooks beat opaque UI transformation steps.

quotes.text: Notebook isn't running code out in the void. It's submitting spark jobs that execute exactly where the data is stored.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains how notebooks, Spark and the Lakehouse work together.

quotes.text: If you document your transformations, tag versions at meaningful checkpoints, and make notes about why code changed, your team doesn't spend days or even weeks guessing at business logic.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Concrete documentation and versioning advice for growing teams.

quotes.text: A necessary step is to build in code review and credential checks from the first notebook onward, not as afterthoughts, but as part of everyday work.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clear recommendation to make review and credential checks routine.

How Lakehouse, notebooks and Spark fit together
The habit that sets pros apart

takeaways: Fabric Notebooks replace scattered Power Query steps, Excel fixes and local scripts with transparent Python or R code that lives next to the Lakehouse data.
Because notebooks submit Spark jobs where the data is stored, cleaning, feature engineering and ML preparation scale without exporting files.
Workspace permissions, audit logs, version control, code review and documentation from day one keep growing notebook estates governed instead of chaotic.
hook: Power BI and Power Query users who are tired of fragile, click-heavy data prep will learn how Fabric Notebooks turn transformations into transparent, repeatable code on the Lakehouse. The episode walks from raw data to ML-ready tables and shows how to keep notebooks governed as teams grow.
